heroLead: West Middletown is one of the oldest villages in Washington County, and a surprising number of its mineral estates are still tied to the original 18th-century land grants.
intro: Some of the oldest deed chains we've ever had to untangle for a family came out of villages like West Middletown, where land has passed down through wills and family agreements going back to before Pennsylvania was even settled this far west. That history is part of what makes small-town mineral ownership here so complicated, and part of why we take the courthouse work seriously.

If you hold minerals under a parcel near West Middletown, there's a good chance your interest sits inside the county's wet gas fairway, which is exactly the ground operators have leased hardest over the last fifteen years.

sections.heading: Old Deeds, New Drilling
paragraphs: West Middletown's historic district status protects the surface, but underneath it the mineral rights have been leased and pooled like anywhere else in Washington County's productive fairway. Deed language from the 1800s often used descriptions that don't match modern surveys, which means confirming your exact interest takes real courthouse work, not a quick database search.
We do that work as part of every offer. If your deed references a boundary marker that no longer exists or a neighbor's name from four owners ago, we've dealt with worse.

sections.heading: Reading Your Royalty Statement Honestly
paragraphs: Most owners near West Middletown who call us are not confused about whether they're being paid. They're confused about why the number keeps shrinking. Post-production deductions, gathering, compression, dehydration, marketing, are the usual answer, and Pennsylvania law lets operators net those costs out as long as the check stays above the one-eighth statutory floor.
We'll go through your actual statement with you and explain, line by line, what each deduction is likely doing to your check, at no cost and with no pressure to sell.

sections.heading: A Single Payment Versus Decades of Deductions
paragraphs: Selling converts an uncertain, declining stream of small checks into one number you control today. For heirs who split an interest three or four ways, that single payment is often easier to manage than four separate small royalty streams running for years.
We structure the offer around your actual net decimal interest, not a guess, so what you see reflects what you actually own.

faqs.question: Does West Middletown's historic designation affect mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No. Historic district status covers surface structures and appearance, not the mineral estate underneath, which is leased and produced the same as elsewhere in Washington County.

faqs.question: My deed uses old boundary language I don't understand. Can you still make an offer?
faqs.answer: Yes. We regularly work with pre-modern deed descriptions and can trace them through the county recorder of deeds to confirm your interest.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum interest size you'll buy?
faqs.answer: We look at fractional and small interests regularly. Bring us your documents and we'll tell you honestly whether it makes sense for us.

faqs.question: Will selling affect my surface property?
faqs.answer: No. A mineral rights sale only involves the subsurface estate; your surface ownership and use of the land are unaffected.
